title: Rounding and Error Intervals
seo_title: Year 9 Rounding Worksheets: Significant Figures, Error Intervals, Truncation and Bounds
standard_text: Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy (for example, to a number of decimal places or significant figures); use inequality notation to specify simple error intervals due to truncation or rounding.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 rounding worksheets: significant figures, decimal places, error intervals for rounding and truncation, upper and lower bounds, and estimation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: For an error interval, add and subtract half of the unit you rounded to.
key_sub: The lower bound uses ≤ and the upper bound uses <.
body_html:
How it works

Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit. To round, look at the next digit: 5 or more rounds up. Keep the place-value zeros: 45,678 to 2 s.f. is 46,000, not 46. Leading zeros in a decimal are not significant: 0.00456 to 2 s.f. is 0.0046.

An error interval shows all the values that round to a given number. If x rounds to 70 to the nearest 10, add and subtract half of 10: 65 ≤ x < 75. If a number is truncated, digits are chopped off, so 3.7 truncated to 1 d.p. gives 3.7 ≤ x < 3.8.

Example

Round 0.06372 to 2 s.f.

The first significant figure is 6; the next digit after 63 is 7.

Answer: 0.064

Example

x = 400 to the nearest 100.

Half of 100 is 50.

Answer: 350 ≤ x < 450

Example

x = 2.4 to 1 d.p.

Half of 0.1 is 0.05.

Answer: 2.35 ≤ x < 2.45

Common mistakes

  • Dropping the zeros when rounding a large number: 3,847 to 1 s.f. is 4,000, not 4.
  • Counting leading zeros as significant figures.
  • Writing ≤ at both ends of an error interval. The upper bound uses <.
  • Using the full unit instead of half of it: 70 to the nearest 10 is not 60 ≤ x < 80.

faq.a: The digits of a number starting from the first non-zero digit. 0.0305 has 3 significant figures: 3, 0 and 5.
The range of values a number could have been before it was rounded or truncated, written with inequalities such as 65 ≤ x < 75.

faq.q: How do I find an error interval for rounding?
faq.a: Halve the unit you rounded to. Subtract it for the lower bound and add it for the upper bound.

faq.q: What is the difference between rounding and truncating?
faq.a: Rounding goes to the nearest value. Truncating just chops off digits, so 3.79 truncated to 1 d.p. is 3.7.

items.q: A number x is rounded to the nearest 5. The result is 420. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: Half of 5 is 2.5. The lower bound is 420 − 2.5 and the upper bound is 420 + 2.5. The upper bound itself would round up, so use <: 417.5 ≤ x < 422.5.

sets.title: Error intervals with decimals and truncation

items.q: x = 37,000, correct to 2 significant figures. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: To 2 significant figures, 37,000 is rounded to the nearest 1,000. Half of that is 500: 36,500 ≤ x < 37,500.

items.q: x = 3,400, correct to 2 significant figures. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: To 2 significant figures, 3,400 is rounded to the nearest 100. Half of that is 50: 3,350 ≤ x < 3,450.

items.q: x = 60, correct to 1 significant figure. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: To 1 significant figure, 60 is rounded to the nearest 10. Half of that is 5: 55 ≤ x < 65.

items.q: x = 61.1, correct to 1 decimal place. What is the error interval for x?
x is truncated to a whole number. The result is 78. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: Truncating chops off digits without rounding, so x is at least 78 and less than 79: 78 ≤ x < 79.

items.q: A rope is 12 m long, to the nearest metre. What is the shortest it could be?
items.e: Half of 1 m is 0.5 m, so the lower bound is 12 − 0.5 = 11.5 m.

items.q: A square has side 6 cm, to the nearest cm. What is the upper bound of its perimeter?
items.e: The side is less than 6.5 cm, so the perimeter is less than 4 × 6.5 = 26 cm.

items.q: A square has side 6 cm, to the nearest cm. What is the lower bound of its area?
items.e: The side is at least 5.5 cm: 5.5² = 30.25 cm².

items.q: A lift can carry 600 kg. Eight people each weigh 75 kg, to the nearest kg. What is the greatest total mass they could have?
items.e: Upper bound of each: 75.5 kg. 8 × 75.5 = 604 kg, so the lift might be overloaded.

items.q: Estimate 4.87 × 21.3 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
Estimate 598 ÷ 0.31 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
Estimate 39.8 × 5.10.49 by rounding to 1 significant figure.
How many significant figures does 0.00720 have?
items.e: Leading zeros do not count; the trailing zero after 72 does: 7, 2, 0 is 3.

items.q: What is 0.04962 rounded to 2 significant figures?
items.e: The first two significant figures are 4 and 9; the next digit is 6, so 49 rounds up to 50: 0.050. Keep the final zero to show 2 s.f.

items.q: The population of a town is 45,000 to 2 significant figures. What is the smallest it could be?
items.e: To 2 s.f. it is rounded to the nearest 1,000. Half is 500: 45,000 − 500 = 44,500.

items.q: A car travels 100 km, to the nearest km, in 2 hours, to the nearest hour. What is the upper bound of its average speed?
items.e: Greatest speed = greatest distance ÷ least time = 100.5 ÷ 1.5 = 67 km/h. Using 99.5 ÷ 2.5 gives the least speed, about 40 km/h.

items.q: A shelf is 80 cm long, to the nearest cm. Books are 4 cm thick, to the nearest mm. Can 20 books always fit?
c: No, the books could be up to 81 cm in total
items.e: Shelf could be 79.5 cm. Books could be 4.05 cm each: 20 × 4.05 = 81 cm. No, they might not fit.

items.q: Which is the error interval for a number that rounds to 3.6 to 1 decimal place?
Why is the upper bound written with < and not ≤?
c: Because the upper bound itself would round up
Because the lower bound uses < too
It is just a convention with no reason
items.e: For example 6.5 rounds to 7, not 6, so 6.5 is not included: because the upper bound itself would round up.

items.q: A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm, both to the nearest cm. What is the lower bound of its area?
Round 299,700 to 2 significant figures.
items.e: The first two figures are 2 and 9; the next is 9, so 29 rounds up to 30, then add the zeros: 300,000.

items.q: A time of 9.8 seconds is truncated to 1 decimal place. What is the greatest the real time could be?
items.e: Truncating means it is at least 9.8 and less than 9.9: just under 9.9 seconds.

items.q: Leo rounds 0.0306 to 1 significant figure and writes 0. What should the answer be?
items.e: The first significant figure is 3 (in the hundredths). 0.03.

items.q: A bag holds 25 kg to the nearest kg. How many bags of 25 kg are needed for a load of exactly 500 kg, in the worst case?
items.e: The least a bag might hold is 24.5 kg. 500 ÷ 24.5 = 20.4…, so in the worst case 21 bags are needed.

items.q: Which number is 7,850 rounded to 2 significant figures?
items.e: The first two figures are 7 and 8; the next is 5, so round up: 7,900.
